standard: WCAG 2.2 AA (and 2.3.3, held as a rule)

jobs.use: The thing you touched answers: hover, press, a toggle or checkbox, a selected row — colour, fill and border, never movement
Content changing where it is: a panel expanding or collapsing, a tab panel, an item added to or removed from a list, a value replaced
What opens over the page without blocking it: menus, popovers, tooltips, date pickers, toasts, the navigation drawer (elevation.floating)
What blocks the page until it is answered: dialogs and sheets, with the scrim fading in behind (elevation.modal)
Drawing the eye to something that changed on its own: a live value that updated, a row that just arrived, a saved field — a tint that fades, once
Work in progress: the loading indicator turns while it runs (in reduced motion it pulses slowly instead) and stops when the work is done

curves.name: exit

curves.name: standard
curves.use: Something changing where it is: a hover, a panel opening, a tab, a highlight fading

rule.formula: duration = 100ms + 37.5ms × √(distance in px), rounded down to 50ms; leaving takes two thirds of arriving (rounded down to 50ms, never under 100ms)

reduced.what: Fade only: no job moves (every distance is 0), transitions fade in 100ms or less, the loading indicator stops turning and pulses every 2000ms, highlights fade as before (a fade is not movement).
how: tokens.css switches to the reduced values when the reader's system asks for less motion (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)
data-motion="reduced" (or "full") on <html> is the reader's own setting in the product; on any container it previews a mode
Figma: a frame set to the Motion collection's reduced mode

ready.from: below: it rises into place while the scrim fades in

ready.html: <nav data-shell="nav" data-open> in .ds-shell (below the breakpoint where it goes inline)
ready.from: its own side (the start side; flipped right to left)

loading.rule: Shows only while work runs and stops when it ends; after 5 seconds, show progress in words or a bar. In reduced motion it pulses to 0.65 opacity — the lowest that keeps color.fg.icon ≥ 3:1 on every surface

highlight.rule: Once per change, at most once per 1000ms; text on the tint stays ≥ 4.5:1 (M5)

feedback.css: transition: background-color var(--ds-motion-feedback-duration) var(--ds-motion-feedback-easing), border-color var(--ds-motion-feedback-duration) var(--ds-motion-feedback-easing), color var(--ds-motion-feedback-duration) var(--ds-motion-feedback-easing);
feedback.tailwind: transition-colors (Tailwind's default duration and curve are motion.feedback in tailwind.theme.css)

classes.use: Menus, popovers, tooltips: drop in from above with motion.floating, leave with its exit (data-layer="toast": up from the bottom)
classes.tailwind: popover (top layer); nothing to add — tokens.css animates [popover].ds-floating

classes.use: A <dialog> opened with showModal(): rises in with motion.modal while the scrim fades, leaves with its exit
The loading indicator: one turn per motion.loading cycle while work runs; in reduced motion a slow pulse
A tint (color.bg.brand-subtle) that fades over motion.highlight, once, when something changed on its own

checks.title: Reduced motion is fade only: nothing moves, transitions fade in 100ms or less, the loading indicator pulses instead of turning
Nothing flashes: a highlight takes ≥ 334ms and no loop changes brightness more than 3 times a second
Duration follows distance: 100ms + 37.5ms × √px rounded down to 50ms, nothing over 32px or 300ms; leaving takes two thirds of arriving; a loop turns at most once a second
No jumps: every curve stays under 2.5× its average speed; arriving lands at rest, leaving starts from rest, changing in place does both
Loops and highlights stay readable: the loading indicator never pulses below 3:1; text stays ≥ 4.5:1 on the highlight tint
Ready transitions: menus, popovers, toasts, the drawer and dialogs open and close with their motion jobs in tokens.css — tokens only, focus rings never animated

rules.rule: Durations and curves come from a job: transition-duration and animation-duration are var(--ds-motion-<job>-duration) (or -exit-duration), timing functions var(--ds-motion-<job>-easing) (or -exit-easing). No ms or s numbers, no ease, ease-in-out or cubic-bezier() written by hand, no Tailwind duration-300 or ease-in-out (Tailwind: ease-<job> and duration-(--ds-motion-<job>-duration)).
rules.why: A number belongs to no job: reduced motion can't shorten it, and nobody can tell what it is for.

rules.rule: Name what transitions: never transition: all (Tailwind transition-all) — list the properties. Never transition outline or outline-offset, and never animate a focus indicator: focus rings appear at once.
rules.why: all animates whatever happens to change — layout, the focus ring, colours in forced colours — and a ring that fades in is missing for its first frames.

rules.rule: Move only by a job's distance, on one axis: translate by var(--ds-motion-<job>-distance) (or calc(-1 * …)). No px, %, vw or vh distances, no scale, rotate or skew, no animated top, left, margin, width or height.
rules.why: Reduced motion sets every distance to 0: movement written any other way keeps moving for people who asked it to stop. Nothing travels more than 32px.

rules.rule: Every animation has a reduced path: keyframes that move (transform, translate, rotate, scale, position) run only inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) or move by the job distances; a reduced block never keeps movement. Tailwind: motion-safe: in front of anything that moves.
rules.why: The reduced mode can only switch off what goes through its tokens.

rules.rule: Opening and closing use the ready transitions: menus, popovers and tooltips are .ds-floating popovers, toasts .ds-floating data-layer="toast", dialogs <dialog class="ds-modal"> opened with showModal(). Don't add transitions or animations of your own to them, and don't animate them with JavaScript.
rules.why: tokens.css already opens and closes them with the right job, keeps them shown and in the top layer while they leave, and only fades them in reduced motion.

rules.rule: One loop: the loading indicator (.ds-loading), shown only while work runs. Any other infinite animation (animation-iteration-count: infinite, Tailwind animate-*) needs a visible pause or stop control, or must end within 5 seconds. Work that can take longer than 5 seconds shows progress in words or a bar, not only a spinner.
rules.why: Motion that runs on beside content pulls the eye away from it, and for some people makes reading impossible.

rules.rule: Nothing flashes: no animation that switches visibility or swings brightness (opacity, colour, background, filter) in a cycle shorter than 334ms, no blinking text, no <marquee> or <blink>.
rules.why: More than three flashes in a second can trigger seizures.

rules.rule: Highlights fade once: a value or row that changed on its own takes .ds-highlight (a tint fading over motion.highlight), at most once per highlight. Never shake, bounce or pulse something to get attention, and never roll digits.
rules.why: A repeated highlight becomes a flash; a shaking field moves for people who asked it not to and tells a screen reader nothing.

rules.rule: Nothing moves with scrolling or on its own: no parallax, no scroll-linked movement (animation-timeline: scroll() or view() that moves things, scroll handlers that translate), scroll-behavior: smooth only inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), no autoplaying video or carousel without pause controls.
rules.why: Movement tied to scrolling is the strongest trigger of motion sickness on the web; autoplay moves beside the content people are reading.

rules.rule: Never redefine motion variables in app code (--ds-motion-*). Set data-motion only from the reader's own setting — never data-motion="full" by default. Add a product job in the engine config (motion.jobs) and build.
rules.why: An overridden job skips the checks for reduced motion, flashes and jumps; a page that forces full motion overrides what the reader asked their system for.

decisions.what: Does it need motion at all
decisions.question: What would people miss without it?
answers: Nothing — it would only look livelier
no motion: it changes at once
That the thing they touched heard them
motion.feedback — colour, fill or border, in 100ms; never movement
Where content went or came from (a panel opening, an item removed)
motion.change
That something opened over the page, and from where
motion.floating or motion.modal — ready in tokens.css
That something changed on its own while they looked elsewhere
motion.highlight — once
That work is still going
motion.loading (.ds-loading) — and progress in words or a bar once it runs past 5 seconds

answers: A menu or popover from its button
.ds-floating does it: it drops in from above, toward where it opens
A toast from the edge it sits on

The navigation drawer

A dialog
dialog.ds-modal does it: it rises into place while the scrim fades in
Content changing in place
the way it grows (down as a panel opens) by motion.change.distance — or not at all
Anything

decisions.question: Is it something people are reading or steering by?
answers: The focus ring
it appears at once (tokens.css draws it; never in a transition list)
Text being read
never moves on its own: no auto-advancing carousels, no rolling digits, no marquees
The page while it scrolls
nothing moves with the scroll: no parallax, no scroll-linked movement
A field with an error
a message and the state border (Border foundation) — never a shake
Something that must get attention
its position and a highlight once — never a pulse or bounce that repeats

mistakes.mistake: transition: all 0.3s ease on a button
mistakes.measured: it animates every property that changes — the focus ring and the layout too — for 300ms, 3× the feedback job, and still 300ms in reduced motion
mistakes.fixValue: transition: background-color, border-color and color at var(--ds-motion-feedback-duration) (100ms), var(--ds-motion-feedback-easing)

mistakes.mistake: A curve that starts at full speed (cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0, 1))
mistakes.measured: its first frame covers 47% of a 4px menu move and 36% of a 16px dialog move (5.8px), then it crawls: a jump, not an arrival — its starting speed has no limit
mistakes.fixValue: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.5, 0.4, 1): never above 2.5× the average speed; the dialog's first frame is 2.6px of 16px

mistakes.mistake: A dialog sliding in from off the screen (translate: 0 100vh)
mistakes.measured: on an 800px-tall window it travels 800px in 300ms (2667px a second), 25× the 32px limit — and reduced motion can't stop it unless it is written twice
mistakes.fixValue: rises 16px in 250ms; in reduced motion it only fades (100ms)

mistakes.mistake: A spinner at animation: spin 0.6s linear infinite
mistakes.measured: 1.7 turns a second, and it keeps turning in reduced motion
mistakes.fixValue: one turn in 1000ms; in reduced motion a pulse every 2000ms that never drops below 3:1

mistakes.measured: 3.3 cycles a second — over the three flashes a second of WCAG 2.3.1 for any area large and contrasty enough to count
mistakes.fixValue: the indicator turns once a second; a skeleton stays still, or pulses at most at the reduced pace (2000ms)

mistakes.mistake: Shaking a field to show an error
mistakes.measured: it moves back and forth in reduced motion, tells a screen reader nothing, and is gone before some people look
mistakes.fix: an error message and the state border
mistakes.fixValue: the message names the problem (aria-describedby), the border widens to its state (Border foundation); .ds-highlight once if the field is out of view

mistakes.measured: every in-page link and every focus jump glides the whole page — for people with reduced motion too
mistakes.fixValue: put the smooth scrolling inside it, or leave it out
